security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are Markdown false positives; ten findings correctly identify documented browser-use CLI invocations. The skill also promotes stealth-enabled cloud browsers for avoiding captchas or rate limits and permits automatic use of an existing SSO session, which require stronger authorization safeguards.

remediation.issue: Cloud-browser guidance promotes stealth settings and managed IPs when captchas or rate limits are likely.
remediation.suggestion: Remove avoidance language and require users to respect site terms, rate limits, and captcha challenges instead of attempting to bypass them.

remediation.issue: Existing signed-in SSO can be used automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before using any authenticated browser session or SSO identity, including a clearly named target account.

remediation.issue: Browser CLI commands can control authenticated browser sessions and cloud instances.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before navigation that can submit data, access private content, create cloud browsers, or incur charges; keep the existing shutdown confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: Automation guidance for captcha and rate-limit avoidance
semantic_findings.description: The cloud-browser guidance recommends managed IPs and stealth settings when captchas, blocking, or repeated automated visits are likely. This can facilitate evasion of website anti-automation controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly connects clean managed IPs and stealth settings with avoiding captcha walls and rate limits.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic use of existing signed-in SSO session
semantic_findings.description: The skill permits automatic use of available SSO when Chrome is already signed in. A signed-in browser can expose account data or initiate actions without a separate confirmation for that account.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit, although it also requires stopping for passwords, MFA, consent, and ambiguous account choices.

content.user_title: Automate Chrome Tasks with Browser Use
content.value_statement: Browser tasks can be slow and difficult to repeat reliably. This skill controls Chrome or Chromium through CDP for guided automation, inspection, testing, and capture workflows.
actual_capabilities: Attach to a running Chrome or Chromium CDP endpoint.
Open browser tabs and inspect page state with the browser-use CLI.
Find page elements through the accessibility tree and interact with coordinates.
Capture screenshots, recordings, and videos when recording is enabled.
Connect to named remote browser daemons and close them after confirmation.
Use CDP and page inspection helpers for DOM extraction and debugging.
limitations: Requires Chrome or Chromium with remote debugging enabled for local control.
Cannot safely complete password, MFA, consent, or ambiguous account-selection steps automatically.
Cloud browser use requires Browser Use authentication and may incur charges.
Website permissions, terms, rate limits, and captchas can restrict automation.

use_cases.title: Repeat browser regression checks
use_cases.description: Run a defined browser workflow and verify page state after navigation or interaction.

use_cases.title: Investigate a web interface
use_cases.description: Inspect accessibility data, page state, and DOM details to diagnose a browser issue.

use_cases.title: Capture a product demonstration
use_cases.description: Record a permitted browser workflow and produce evidence for a support or product task.

prompt_templates.title: Open and inspect a page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open https://example.com in my local browser and summarize the page title and visible main sections. Ask before interacting with forms.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a user journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Test the public navigation path from the homepage to the pricing page. Report each page title and stop before any login or form submission.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an interface issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the accessibility tree for the checkout button on this already open page. Explain why it may not be clickable and do not submit any purchase.

prompt_templates.title: Capture approved evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: With my permission, record the current public product walkthrough. Stop recording after verification and tell me the exact recording location.

output: Found three plan cards and a comparison section.
No login or form interaction was attempted.
The accessibility tree lists Submit as a disabled button.
The page indicates that a required email field is empty.

best_practices: Confirm the target site, account, and intended action before accessing authenticated content.
Prefer the accessibility tree and targeted checks over broad screenshots or raw page dumps.
Stop cloud browser instances after work and verify the shutdown decision with the user.
anti_patterns: Do not use automation to bypass captchas, rate limits, website terms, or access controls.
Do not enter passwords, MFA codes, consent choices, or select an ambiguous account without explicit user approval.
Do not leave remote browsers running without explaining potential charges and asking for confirmation.

faq.question: What browser does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls Chrome or Chromium through the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

faq.question: Does local browser control need setup?
faq.answer: Yes. Chrome remote debugging must be enabled and the user may need to approve its permission prompt.

faq.question: Can it use a cloud browser?
faq.answer: Yes. Cloud browsers require Browser Use authentication and may incur charges until stopped or timed out.

faq.question: Can it sign in for me?
faq.answer: It should stop for passwords, MFA, consent, or unclear account selection. Confirm any authenticated session before use.

faq.question: Can it record browser work?
faq.answer: Yes, when recording is enabled or requested. Recordings must use the returned recording path for reliable evidence.

faq.question: Can it bypass captchas or rate limits?
faq.answer: No. Use the skill only in ways that respect website terms, permissions, captchas, and rate limits.
